items.title: Character.AI Bankruptcy: Watch for Phishing Emails
items.summary: Character.AI — the popular AI chatbot platform — just filed for bankruptcy today. Scammers will jump on this immediately. Expect fake emails claiming to be from "Character.AI Support" about account closures, data retrieval, or refunds. They'll include links that steal your login

items.title: Windows has free built-in ransomware protection — turn on Controlled Folder Access in Windows Security
items.summary: Windows 10 and 11 include Controlled Folder Access, a free ransomware shield that stops unauthorized programs from encrypting your files. It's off by default. Turn it on: Open Windows Security (press Start and type "Windows Security") → Virus & threat protection → Manage ransomware protection → Turn on Controlled Folder Access.

items.title: Clearwave Fiber brings 100% fiber internet to Lake City — check your address at clearwavefiber.com
items.summary: Clearwave Fiber now offers 100% fiber internet in Lake City with symmetrical speeds up to 1 Gbps, no contracts, no data caps. Check if your address qualifies: go to clearwavefiber.com/address-search and enter your Lake City address. Plans start at 100 Mbps for $50/month.

items.title: Windows 11 has a free built-in screen recorder — press Win+G to capture anything
items.summary: Windows 11 includes the Xbox Game Bar, a free screen recorder that captures any app window with audio. Press the Windows key + G to open it, then click the record button (or press Win+Alt+R). Videos save to Videos\Captures. No download, no watermark, no time limit.

items.title: Alert Clay sends free emergency texts for hurricanes and evacuations — sign up at alertclay.org
items.summary: Clay County's free Alert Clay system sends emergency texts for hurricanes, evacuations, boil-water notices, and other threats. Sign up at claycountygov.com/community/alert-clay or text your zip code to 888777. You choose text, email, or phone call alerts.

items.title: CISA adds two actively exploited Zammad vulnerabilities to danger list — update your software now at zammad.org
items.summary: CISA added Zammad Session Fixation (CVE-2026-102489) and Improper Privilege Management (CVE-2026-102490) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 2. If your organization uses Zammad helpdesk software, update immediately at zammad.org. Federal agencies have until October 11 to patch.

items.title: Windows 11 has a free built-in ransomware shield — Controlled Folder Access stops file encryption in seconds
items.summary: Open Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Manage ransomware protection > turn on Controlled folder access. Free, built into Windows 11, protects Documents, Pictures, Desktop folders automatically. Allow trusted apps if they get blocked.

items.title: Clay Electric outage texts tell you the power is out before your neighbor knows — free at clayelectric.com
items.summary: Sign up for free outage alerts at clayelectric.com or text OUT to 855-939-3840. Get real-time text/email alerts the moment power goes out at your address. The MyClayElectric app also shows a live outage map.

items.title: Windows 11 24H2 loses security updates October 13 — check your version at Settings > System > About and upgrade free
items.summary: Open Settings > System > About > check Windows version. If you're on 24H2 Home/Pro, go to Settings > Windows Update and upgrade to 25H2. Free, automatic, keeps you protected. Deadline is tomorrow, October 13.

items.title: Windows 11 Storage Sense automatically frees 5-50 GB monthly — turn it on in Settings > System > Storage
items.summary: Open Settings > System > Storage > turn on Storage Sense. Windows automatically deletes temp files, empties Recycle Bin, and cleans Downloads folder on a schedule you set. Free, built-in, no download needed. Runs when disk space is low or daily/weekly/monthly.

items.title: Fake Virus Popup Scam
items.summary:
That "Virus Detected" Popup Is a Total Fake.

You're browsing the web and suddenly a loud siren blares from your speakers. A giant red popup fills the screen: "WARNING: 47 VIRUS DETECTED. Your files are being stolen. Call Microsoft Support NOW: 1-888-XXX-XXXX."

Here's the truth: Microsoft doesn't work this way. That popup is a webpage — just a picture. It can't see your files. It can't hurt anything. It's a lie.
